evals.prompt: Saya mau bikin app buat tracking pengeluaran freelancer. Jadi freelancer bisa masukin expense, attach receipt foto, terus di akhir bulan bisa generate laporan buat pajak. Target market freelancer Indonesia yang penghasilannya 10-50jt/bulan.
evals.expected_output: Should produce structured product documents starting with Product Overview, following the 5-phase workflow (Decompose > Scope > Architect > Detail > Validate). Should ask clarifying questions first before producing documents. Output should be specific to this expense tracker, not generic.
expectations: Agent asks at least 2 clarifying questions before producing documents
Output mentions specific Indonesian tax context (PPh 21, PPh 23, or similar)
Tech stack recommendations include specific reasoning, not just names
No sentences that could be swapped into a different product's documentation unchanged
Agent follows the 5-phase sequence and does not skip Decompose or Scope
MVP scope is explicitly defined and separates v1 from future features
Output does NOT contain filler phrases like 'comprehensive solution' or 'robust platform' or 'cutting-edge'

evals.prompt: I want to build a browser extension that helps people compare prices across e-commerce sites. When you're on Tokopedia looking at a product, it shows prices from Shopee, Bukalapak, etc. Maybe also price history graphs.
evals.expected_output: Should address browser extension-specific architecture (content scripts, background workers, popup). Should identify the scraping/API challenge as a core technical risk. Should scope MVP aggressively - probably just 2 platforms to start.
expectations: Architecture addresses browser extension components (content script, background service worker, popup)
Identifies web scraping legality or API availability as a risk or constraint
MVP scope limits to 2-3 e-commerce platforms, not all of them
Does NOT recommend microservices or over-engineered backend for what is essentially a client-side tool
Price history feature is explicitly scoped as v2 or later, not crammed into MVP
Tech stack includes specific browser extension framework reasoning (Manifest V3, Plasmo, WXT, or similar)

evals.prompt: Plan MVP untuk SaaS yang bisa bikin invoice otomatis dari data project di Jira. Jadi consulting firm bisa track time di Jira, terus generate invoice langsung dari situ. Target market consulting firm kecil 5-20 orang.
evals.expected_output: Should connect Jira API integration as the core technical challenge. Should address billing models, multi-tenant architecture at small scale. Should be opinionated about tech choices with reasoning.
expectations: Addresses Jira API integration specifics (OAuth, webhooks, or Atlassian Connect)
Data model includes relationship between Jira worklogs and invoice line items
Recommends a monolith or simple architecture, NOT microservices for a 5-20 person target
Discusses multi-tenancy approach with specific recommendation
Tech recommendations include version numbers or recency indicators showing research awareness
Output includes acceptance criteria that a developer could test against

evals.prompt: Kita mau bikin platform telemedicine untuk rumah sakit di Indonesia. Pasien bisa konsultasi online sama dokter, ada video call, resep digital, dan integrasi sama sistem rekam medis rumah sakit (SIMRS). Target 50 rumah sakit dalam 2 tahun. Tim kita ada 4 squad.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger Enterprise mode (Phase 0). Should ask about HIPAA/local health regulations, existing SIMRS systems, security requirements. Should produce architecture with compliance, multi-team coordination, and security depth.
expectations: Agent asks 'MVP atau Enterprise?' or directly identifies this as enterprise-level based on context
Agent asks follow-up questions about compliance (PP 71/2019, health data regulations)
Agent asks about existing SIMRS systems and integration constraints
Agent asks about security requirements for health data
Architecture includes STRIDE threat model or security architecture section
Data classification is applied (PHI as Restricted)
Multi-team coordination is addressed (4 squads, service boundaries, RACI)
Audit trail requirements are specified for patient data access
Does NOT skip compliance requirements to v2 — health data protection is MVP scope
References Indonesian health regulations (PP 71/2019, Permenkes) not just HIPAA

evals.prompt: Build a B2B SaaS for enterprise expense management. SOC2 compliance required, integrates with SAP and Oracle ERP, 3 engineering teams will build it. Target: Fortune 500 companies. Need to handle PCI-DSS for corporate card data.
evals.expected_output: Should activate full enterprise mode. Should address SOC2, PCI-DSS, multi-team architecture, legacy ERP integration patterns, and operational readiness.
expectations: Agent identifies this as Enterprise and activates enterprise mode
SOC2 requirements are reflected in architecture (audit logging, access control, change management)
PCI-DSS is addressed — recommends tokenization or delegating card handling to compliant processor
Integration patterns for SAP/Oracle are discussed (middleware, API gateway, or integration platform)
Multi-team coordination is explicit (3 teams, service boundaries, integration contracts)
SLO/SLI definitions are included or recommended
Deployment strategy includes rollback and operational readiness gates
Does NOT treat this as a simple monolith — acknowledges scale requires thoughtful service design
Architecture decisions reference actual enterprise integration tools (MuleSoft, Workato, or similar)

evals.prompt: Mau bikin fintech lending platform. P2P lending buat UMKM Indonesia. Harus comply sama OJK, ada credit scoring, disbursement, dan collection. Tim 2 squad, target launch 6 bulan.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger enterprise mode due to OJK compliance. Should address financial regulations, credit scoring architecture, payment integration, and security for financial data.
expectations: Agent identifies OJK compliance as enterprise-level requirement
References specific OJK regulations (POJK for P2P lending, sandbox requirements)
Data classification includes financial data as Confidential/Restricted
Credit scoring architecture is discussed (ML model, data sources, fairness considerations)
Payment/disbursement integration addresses Indonesian payment rails (bank transfer, e-wallet)
Security architecture includes fraud detection considerations
Audit trail for all financial transactions is specified
Multi-team scoping addresses 2 squads with clear boundaries
Timeline acknowledges OJK licensing process may affect launch date
Does NOT recommend generic 'use Stripe' — addresses Indonesia-specific payment landscape

evals.prompt: I want to build a simple todo app for personal use. Just me using it. Maybe share with my wife later.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger enterprise mode. Should keep it extremely simple. Should actively resist overengineering.
expectations: Agent does NOT ask enterprise questions — this is clearly MVP/personal
Architecture is minimal (SQLite or local storage, no microservices)
Does NOT recommend Kubernetes, message queues, or distributed databases
Does NOT add compliance, audit logging, or multi-team coordination
Scope is aggressively small — basic CRUD for todos
Tech stack is boring and simple (maybe just a single framework)
Agent might even suggest existing tools (Notion, Todoist) before building custom

evals.prompt: We're building an enterprise HR platform that needs to handle employee data across 15 countries. GDPR for EU employees, local labor laws per country. Integrates with existing Active Directory. 6 engineering teams.
evals.expected_output: Should activate enterprise mode with heavy compliance focus. Should address multi-region data residency, GDPR, cross-team coordination at scale, and AD integration.
expectations: Agent activates enterprise mode and asks about specific countries/regulations
GDPR is addressed with specific architectural impact (data residency, right to erasure, consent)
Multi-region data residency is a core architecture concern
Active Directory integration is addressed (SCIM, SAML, or direct LDAP)
6-team coordination includes RACI or explicit ownership model
Service boundaries are defined to allow team autonomy
Data classification covers employee PII across jurisdictions
Architecture addresses 'which data stays in which region' explicitly
Does NOT produce a simple monolith — acknowledges multi-region requires distributed design
Operational readiness includes incident response for data breaches (GDPR 72-hour notification)
